single_new_mechanism.scientific_reason: TOPA and the sealed R33 counterexample show that the Tseitin core is a parity/affine object. Schaefer-type affine satisfiability is polynomial-time solvable by Gaussian elimination, so R34 tests one structural terminal recognizer rather than adding another CNF deletion heuristic.
recognition_contract: Run the R33 safe-reduction stack byte-for-byte first.
Invoke the new mechanism only on a nonterminal R33 STALLED_STACK_LEAN_CORE.
Group every remaining CNF clause by its exact absolute variable set.
A group is an XOR bundle only when its clauses are exactly the complete set of wrong-parity assignments for one affine equation over that variable set.
The entire remaining formula must partition into recognized XOR bundles. Partial recognition is not enough; no hybrid SAT search is permitted in R34.
Solve the recovered system over GF(2) by deterministic Gaussian elimination.

certificate_contract.UNSAT: Carry source-equation combination bits through row operations; a contradiction certificate must re-check as XOR of selected source equations = 0 = 1 without a SAT solver.
certificate_contract.SAT: Emit one GF(2) assignment and re-check it against every recovered affine equation and every original CNF clause.
certificate_contract.recognition: Each recovered equation must be independently re-expanded to its forbidden parity assignments and match the source CNF group exactly.

single_new_mechanism.complexity_contract: Recognition and GF(2) elimination must use an explicitly counted polynomial number of bit/row operations in numbers of active variables, clauses and equations. No enumeration of 2^n assignments is allowed.

frozen_controls.expected: All three R33 semantic controls remain PASS and the R33 rule stack behavior is unchanged.
